findings.issue: When a remote's refs/remotes/<r>/HEAD resolves inside its own remote, remoteDefaultRefs stops excluding that remote's main and master, which the previous code always excluded.
findings.consequence: In a gitflow repo whose origin/HEAD names develop (or one whose origin/HEAD is stale after a master-to-main rename), a branch cut from a fresh origin/main while local main lags takes merged main commits — and their runs and findings — back into its range, the pull-in the exclusion exists to prevent.

findings.issue: The comment above Load's remote listing still says the remote defaults are refs/remotes/<remote>/main|master.
findings.consequence: Readers are told the wrong default-branch rule.

findings.issue: internal/status tests obtain an unknown scope from a bare t.TempDir() and assume TMPDIR is outside a repository, as the findings tests did before (e).
findings.consequence: With TMPDIR inside a checkout, 11 status tests fail; nothing fails in a normal environment.

findings.issue: The --all warning wording is swapped in emit() by a string match on a constant built in buildFor.
findings.consequence: A future rewording can silently keep the self-referential hint.

findings.issue: refs/remotes/<r>/HEAD can be pointed at a remote-tracking ref of one's own pushed branch, subtracting it from the range.
findings.consequence: Legacy range-only rows could fall out of scope; not a new capability (update-ref of refs/remotes/origin/main already does it).

verdict.reasoning: The diff intentionally changes the policy from always treating main/master as defaults to using a valid remote HEAD target, with main/master only as fallback. The implementation matches the updated function contract. The finding objects to that intended behavior and provides no evidence that main/master must remain excluded in addition to the actual default branch; its downstream range claim is not verifiable from the shown diff.

The supplied diff does not show the alleged comment above Load's remote listing. The only relevant comment shown is updated to describe symbolic remote HEAD resolution with main/master fallback, matching the implementation. Without the text of another stale comment, the claimed documentation defect is not verifiable from the evidence provided.

The diff only adds output-content assertions to an existing test and does not introduce or modify t.TempDir(), TMPDIR handling, or repository-scope discovery. The proposed finding concerns an unshown, apparently pre-existing test-environment assumption and provides no repository search record or code evidence tying it to the added lines, so it is not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

The current code constructs the warning with the same elsewhereHint constant that emit() replaces, so the match is guaranteed for the shown path and --all receives the intended wording. A hypothetical future edit that stops using the shared constant is speculative and not a defect present in this diff.

The diff intentionally defines a remote’s default branch from its local refs/remotes/<r>/HEAD symref, with validation that the target remains under that remote. The proposed finding merely observes that a user who can mutate local Git refs can influence scope, and it concedes equivalent influence already existed by changing remote-tracking refs. It does not identify a new correctness or security defect introduced by this change.
